title: Apple’s updated App Store rules go after ‘nudify’ AI apps
content:
Apple’s App Store rules now more explicitly ban so-called “nudify” apps that generate intimate images of people without their consent using AI tools.
Apple’s updated App Store rules go after ‘nudify’ AI apps
The terms more explicitly ban apps that create ‘nonconsensual intimate imagery.’
The rule changes follow significant criticism toward Apple after X users used Grok earlier this year to make nonconsensual, sexualized deepfakes, including minors. Apple didn’t pull X or Grok from the App Store, though it told senators that it threatened to yank Grok. At Apple’s WWDC event in June, protestors also called on Apple to “remove Grok, X, and all nudify technology from the App Store,” and in July, a San Francisco city attorney ordered Apple to remove 13 “nudify” apps, which it said it did.
As part of updates announced Friday, Apple says that developers “must proactively prevent and remove” nonconsensual, sexual images as part of its content moderation requirements for App Store apps. Developers who “fail to implement adequate safeguards” or “don’t remedy violations after notice” may be removed from the App Store. Apple also clarified a rule that bars “bait-and-switch” apps, or apps that add or change features, including “nudification,” after they have been approved.
Apple’s rules also more clearly spell out that any apps that “facilitate human trafficking or the exploitation of children” will be pulled from the App Store and “blocked from alternative distribution.”

report.summary: Apple updated App Store rules to explicitly ban AI 'nudify' apps and require developers to prevent nonconsensual intimate imagery.
report.background: The change follows mounting pressure over AI-generated nonconsensual intimate imagery. Earlier this year, X users used Grok to create sexualized deepfakes, including of minors, prompting criticism that Apple continued to host X and Grok. Apple told senators it had threatened to remove Grok, but it did not pull the apps. In June, protesters at WWDC urged Apple to remove Grok, X, and nudify technology; in July, San Francisco's city attorney ordered Apple to remove 13 nudify apps, which Apple said it did. Apple's guidelines already barred certain sexual content, but the new language makes obligations more explicit for AI image generation and app review. The update also arrives as app stores face growing scrutiny over deepfake harms and as Apple prepares to allow alternative app distribution in some regions, raising questions about how rules extend beyond its own store.
key_points: Apple now explicitly prohibits apps that generate nonconsensual intimate imagery, often called 'nudify' apps. The guidelines require developers to 'proactively prevent and remove' such content, turning content moderation into an ongoing App Store obligation rather than a one-time review checkbox.

Enforcement has teeth: Apple says developers who fail to implement adequate safeguards or don't fix violations after notice may be removed from the App Store. That puts pressure on AI app makers to build detection, reporting, and takedown systems before launch.

Apple closed a 'bait-and-switch' loophole. Apps cannot add or change features—including nudification—after approval. This targets developers who ship benign apps and later enable explicit AI features to evade review.

The rules also state that apps facilitating human trafficking or child sexual exploitation will be pulled and 'blocked from alternative distribution.' That signals Apple wants its safety rules to follow apps beyond the main App Store, especially as sideloading expands.

The update follows criticism over X and Grok, WWDC protests, and a San Francisco city attorney order to remove 13 nudify apps. Apple had already removed some apps, but the new language sets a clearer, reusable standard for AI-generated abuse.
report.impact: For AI developers, the update raises compliance costs: image-generation and editing apps need safety classifiers, abuse reporting, age controls, and rapid takedown workflows, or risk removal. It also clarifies platform liability expectations as deepfake tools proliferate. For the broader AI industry, Apple's move adds pressure on Google Play, cloud providers, and model API vendors to align policies and detection. Regular users may see fewer blatant nudify apps and faster removals, but enforcement will likely be uneven; determined bad actors can move to web tools or sideloaded apps. Victim advocacy groups may welcome the explicit language, though questions remain about appeals, transparency, and how Apple audits 'adequate safeguards.'
report.tools: Follow Apple's App Store Review Guidelines, especially safety and user-generated content sections; Thorn's Safer; StopNCII.org for victim takedown; and open-source NSFW classifiers like NSFWJS and open_nsfw for moderation prototyping. Also watch platform transparency reports and Google Play's evolving deepfake policies.
